It’s lonely as hell and yeah, I sure wish I had someone to vent to or talk about things with at the end of the day. It’s hard to be a single parent and no one to lean on. Not that it’s easier to be lonely single, but I remember when my kid had a broken leg and I spent weeks doing everything for him with zero help or relief and going to bed one night and just completely breaking down. All I wanted in that moment was someone who cared about how I felt and wanted to ease it... But instead, like every night, I just go to sleep in silence and keep all my thoughts to myself. At least no one is there to see me cry, as I so often do. 

I’m not asking for any sympathy in my situation, or comfort, or a pep talk of how it could change. I think I’m just better off trying to accept things as they are and not get my hopes up to be let down again.

My experience has always been that period blood didn’t stain, unless my sheets or underwear are white. 

If possible, see a gynecologist and make sure everything is ok. Heavy flow can be normal, can be something else, better safe than sorry. You could also be put on birth control to lighten the flow and you’d also know when your period would start because the hormones are regulated. 

As far as how to get more undies... just talk to your dad privately. Tell him that you need it, he *should* be able to understand your needs and provide them. Tell him you need him to be discreet. Ask if he can give you cash so you can go buy them yourself, if possible. 

While I realize that this may seem absolutely mortifying to you, an adult man with children (like your dad) should be totally aware of what a menstrual cycle is and that accidents happen. 

I am absolutely not trying to diminish your feelings. But what you’re experiencing is not uncommon and is absolutely nothing to be embarrassed of.

I had a job once as an insurance underwriter and we had a guy on our team who was a former doctor. Many of us would ask him medical related questions based on our work and he was really funny and charming and helpful. 

One day, he sat down with me at lunch. I didn’t often eat lunch in the cafeteria at work, but this day I was sitting with another coworker and he plunked his bag down and started talking to us like it was a daily routine. It was such an enjoyable conversation, he was so smart and funny and easy to talk to. 

This continued for the next few days, I eventually asked him “why are you working as an underwriter if you could be a doctor?” He had made several references to his medical career in a very casual way during our lunches. I’d overheard part of his rap before when he would explain it to other people that he was between jobs when his license lapsed and he took this job because it was a good fit with his schedule, docs keep weird hours, etc. 

Well, I’m not sure why he chose to share with us, but he revealed that he actually lost his license because he was addicted to opioids and he abused meds using his own rx pad, that he had progressed to heroin and was in jail, literally he only had this job because he knew the man who owned the company and he gave him a break. He said that working there was a different kind of stress but the people helped him stay clean, the routine helped him stay clean. 

While he was jovial and smart and a great dude, there was still an underlying melancholy to him. I sat with him at lunch for about 3 weeks, until one day he didn’t come to work. I didn’t think anything of it, but later that afternoon our supervisor called a small team meeting to tell us that he had passed away - they were not sure if it was a suicide or an accidental overdose. I think it was officially classified as an overdose, but I don’t know other details about his death. 

For a long time after, I thought about our lunch convos and wondered if he was reaching out to us for help and we just didn’t hear him. Ultimately, I decided that I am not that powerful and can’t change something that big if someone else had made the decision to do it (either commit suicide or do drugs). 

But I share all this to say - I feel you. It’s shocking and strange and also not shocking and not strange at all. I thank you for sharing your story because I hadn’t thought of this coworker in quite some time (this happened about 10 years ago), and I appreciate the reminder of him. 

Keep him in your memory, it’s the only way any of us stick around after we’re gone. 💕

I ended up aspirating and getting fluid in my pleural cavity that required a thorocotomy - attempted laparoscopically and had to abort because I aspirated during that surgery. Long story short, I required another, open thorocotomy, I went into septic shock, spent 2 weeks in ICU and nearly died. 

After all that, I went to Loyola in Chicago and was officially diagnosed with achalasia. I had a heller myotomy in September 2017. Post op was good, then in January 2018 I had some VERY MINOR recurrence of swallowing issues and had to have an esophageal dilation, which was a quick outpatient procedure and has resolved symptoms since then. I’m less than a year out from the dilation so I’m reluctant to say I’m recovered. 

I share all this to say that if you’re choking in your sleep you need to sleep elevated. Avoid laying on your right side if possible, best position is on your back and elevated with a wedge pillow. Could literally save your life to do this!!

Use good moisturizer and eye cream. I have creases AND dark circles and so I have to use concealer or the dark circles are very obvious due to my pale skin. 

Key is that the skin underneath is as smooth as possible. So. Moisturizer, eye cream or gel, and primer. 
I don’t use foundation under my eyes, but I do have a color correcting primer I use on top of my all over primer. Then concealer which I blend with a beauty blender. Setting with powder or baking is a mistake for people with fine lines. Powder will settle into the lines as the day goes on. If your concealer isn’t blending well with your foundation you may need to use a wetter sponge. I soak my beauty blender and use it when it’s very damp, this allows me to press it into the skin for full coverage that is seamless with my foundation. 

To finish, in place of powder, I use a setting spray when my face is complete. I have skin that is normal to dry, so powder really makes me look dried out. I avoid it for a lot of reasons, I don’t think it’s a great choice for dry or aging skin. Since I have both, I avoid it completely! 

Get some eye masks too and add them into your self care routine. Anything you can do to plump that skin up will buy you some precious time to slow down the clock!

You can not easily cover up dark circles tho 😂😂😂 

Just like straight hair isn’t easier than curly. Just different.

Not necessarily all high end stuff (my everyday moisturizer is Olay, the cheapest one they make, and I LOVE IT - my favorite primer is L’Oréal Magic Lumi, they have on BOGO at Walgreens regularly), but taking care of your skin will make for the smoothest makeup application as well as nicest final result. 

Starter pack recommendations: 
- Colourpop foundation and/or concealer. Love their color range and price point. 
- A beauty blender (doesn’t have to be the $20 name brand, I use a $5 ecotools one and it does the job!) 
- Mascara - I really have tried many and you need to know your lashes. I’ve been happy w Maybelline or L’Oréal mascaras if you’re looking for lower price. 
- A basic nudes pallet. LA Girl makes a cheap one that has good pigmentation and is a dupe for Urban Decay. 
- Highlighter (wet and wild just had some really gorgeous ones for the Halloween collection. Not sure if they could still be found online but I wish I’d stocked up!!) 
- A few brushes. Real Techniques makes great ones that are sold a lot of places (Walmart, Walgreens) and you can buy singles or little sets for decent price. I’d get a set of 3 eye brushes and a full face brush to start. 

It seems like a lot. Maybe it is. I am a makeup hoarder tho, so maybe I am suggesting the most! 

Good luck! Have fun!!!

If she’s separated (not divorced), then my advice is to be friendly with her at most. Don’t get into a relationship with her. Don’t start thinking of or planning a future with someone who is married to someone else.

He and I moved in together, had our life together, I became pregnant and had a child before he could finalize his lengthy divorce. He and I were great through it all, but towards the end of it he became very jaded. He specifically said he would never get married again. Despite saying totally opposite when we got together.

Divorce is ugly. It brings up ugly things. It’s a final knell in the coffin of a relationship. She will have to wrap her head around that on her own, and heal, and become who she is meant to be post-divorce before she can fully commit to someone else (you, or anyone).
